paragraphs.source_en: After leaving Chaya’s residence, Ieyasu could not help laughing several times on the way to Hashiba Hidenaga’s mansion near Jurakudai in Uchino. Hideyoshi’s attendant, fearing that the affair might damage relations between the two sides, had secretly sent warning solely to protect the interests of the people of Sakai. The warning was kindly meant, yet its purpose was to make Ieyasu bow his head to Hideyoshi. Perhaps Hideyoshi himself had ordered it! If Hideyoshi was angry, his younger brother Hidenaga would naturally be angry as well—Ōmandokoro was their mother!

paragraphs.source_en: At Hidenaga’s mansion, the garden trees, earth, and stones were all still new, and autumn frost lay thick upon the ground. Oda Nobukatsu and Oda Uraku, whom Ieyasu had expected to see among those greeting him, were nowhere to be found either. Had Uraku been there, he could have learned the truth of the matter.
